onboarding.title: Set up Nugget
onboarding.offline: The Nugget background service isn't running, so this step can't reach it right now. Skip it and come back later, or start Nugget and this page will catch up.
onboarding.welcome.heading: Welcome to Nugget
onboarding.welcome.lead: Nugget learns from your notes, mail and calendar, and helps you write, find and remember things. It runs on this computer, and you decide what it reads and where anything goes.
onboarding.welcome.stays1: Everything Nugget indexes from your sources, and the knowledge it builds from them
onboarding.welcome.stays2: Your chats and drafts when you use a local model
onboarding.welcome.stays3: Your settings, encrypted with a key kept in your OS keychain
onboarding.welcome.leaves1: Requests to a cloud AI provider, if you set one up with your own key
onboarding.welcome.leaves2: Syncing with accounts you connect, such as Gmail or a CalDAV calendar
onboarding.welcome.leaves3: Model downloads, checked against a signed manifest
onboarding.welcome.ledger: There's no telemetry and no Nugget server in between. Every request that leaves this device is listed on the Privacy page.
onboarding.welcome.time: Setup takes about two minutes. You can skip any step and change everything later.
onboarding.ai.heading: Choose your AI
onboarding.ai.lead: Pick what answers your questions and writes drafts. Small local models always handle sorting and search, whatever you choose here.
onboarding.ai.localBlurb: A local model runs on your computer. Nothing you ask leaves it, and it works offline.
onboarding.ai.byokBlurb: Use Anthropic, OpenAI or any OpenAI-compatible service with your own API key. Requests go straight from this device to that provider.
onboarding.ai.laterBlurb: Search and your knowledge base work without one. Chat and drafting wait until you pick a model.
onboarding.ai.laterDetail: You can choose any time on the Models page, or add a provider to your config file.
onboarding.models.heading: Recommended models
onboarding.models.lead: Picked to run well on most computers. The download is checked before use, and you can keep using Nugget while it runs.
onboarding.models.none: No recommended models are listed in this version's manifest. See the Models page for everything available.
onboarding.models.fit.needs: Needs {ram, number} GB of memory and {disk} of free disk space.
onboarding.models.fit.whyGpu: Recommended for this computer: it has {ram, number} GB of memory, and its {gpu} speeds the model up.
onboarding.models.fit.whyCpu: Recommended for this computer: it has {ram, number} GB of memory. The model runs on the processor, so answers come more slowly than with a graphics card.
onboarding.models.fit.ramTooSmall: This computer has {ram, number} GB of memory; this model needs {need, number} GB and may not run well.
onboarding.models.fit.diskTooSmall: Not enough free disk space: {disk} needed, {free} free.
onboarding.byok.heading: Use your own API key
onboarding.byok.never: Nugget keeps keys out of files. Paste one below and Nugget checks it with the provider, then stores it in your OS keychain; the config file only says where to find it. Or set it up yourself with the steps that follow.
onboarding.byok.manual: Or set it up by hand
onboarding.byok.step1.keychain: In your OS keychain (recommended). Run this, then paste the key when asked:
onboarding.byok.step1.env: Or as an environment variable that the Nugget background service can see:
onboarding.byok.step1.noKey: A server on this computer or your local network usually needs no key. Leave out the api_key line.
onboarding.byok.step2: Add the provider to your config file
onboarding.byok.step2.envSwap: Using an environment variable instead? Write {ref} as the api_key.
onboarding.byok.step3.body: The provider then appears on the Status page, where you can check what it can do.
onboarding.byok.egress: Requests to a cloud provider are recorded in the egress ledger on the Privacy page, and items marked sensitive are never sent.
onboarding.byok.form.heading: Check and save your key
onboarding.byok.form.intro: Prefer not to use the terminal? Paste the key here. Nugget checks it with the provider, stores it in your OS keychain and adds the provider to your config file.
onboarding.byok.form.baseUrlHint: Required for OpenAI-compatible services. It usually ends in /v1.
onboarding.byok.form.modelHint: The model id to use, as the provider names it.
onboarding.byok.form.name: Name
onboarding.byok.form.nameHint: How Nugget refers to this provider: 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits, - or _.
onboarding.byok.form.saved: Key checked and saved. Restart Nugget to start using it.
onboarding.byok.form.error.bad_key: The provider rejected this key. Check that you copied all of it.
onboarding.byok.form.error.wrong_url: Nothing that looks like an AI provider answered at this address. Check the URL (it usually ends in /v1).
onboarding.byok.form.error.no_network: Could not reach the provider. Check your internet connection or the address.
onboarding.byok.form.error.server_error: The provider had a problem answering. Try again in a few minutes.
onboarding.byok.form.error.exists: A provider with this name is already set up. Choose another name.
onboarding.byok.form.error.name: Use 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits, - or _ for the name.
onboarding.source.heading: Add your first source
onboarding.source.lead: A source is somewhere Nugget reads from: a folder, an Obsidian vault, a mailbox or a calendar. It stays where it is; Nugget builds a searchable index on this device and keeps it up to date.
onboarding.source.indexing: {name}: indexing, {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} so far…
onboarding.source.ready: {name}: {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} indexed. Search works now.
onboarding.source.later: You can add and remove sources any time on the Sources page.
onboarding.perm.heading: Permissions, explained
onboarding.perm.lead: Double Tap drafts a reply right where you're typing. To do that, your system has to let Nugget read the text field you're in and type into it. Nothing is requested now: you'll be asked the first time you use Double Tap, and you can say no.
onboarding.perm.mac.ax: Accessibility lets Nugget read the focused text field and insert the draft. Turn it on in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility.
onboarding.perm.mac.input: Input Monitoring lets Nugget notice your trigger key. Only that key is watched; nothing you type is recorded.
onboarding.perm.mac.revoke: You can turn either off at any time in the same place.
onboarding.perm.win.uia: No extra permission is needed. Nugget uses UI Automation, which Windows provides to every app.
onboarding.perm.win.admin: Apps running as administrator can't be read by apps that aren't, so Double Tap won't work in them unless Nugget runs the same way.
onboarding.perm.linux.atspi: AT-SPI, the Linux accessibility bus, lets Nugget read and fill text fields. Most desktops have it on; on GNOME, turn on any accessibility feature or run gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface toolkit-accessibility true.
onboarding.perm.linux.wayland: On Wayland, your desktop asks once before Nugget can use a global shortcut. On X11 no prompt is needed.
onboarding.perm.linux.flatpak: Some apps (for example, some Flatpaks and Electron apps) don't expose their text to AT-SPI; there, Double Tap falls back to the clipboard.
onboarding.perm.scope: Nugget only reads the window you trigger it in, only when you trigger it.
onboarding.trigger.heading: Choose your Double Tap trigger
onboarding.trigger.lead: Press the trigger in any app to get a draft in your voice. Pick something you don't press twice by accident.
onboarding.trigger.doubleTapBlurb: Tap a modifier key twice quickly, without pressing anything else.
onboarding.trigger.chordBlurb: Press several keys together, like a normal shortcut.
onboarding.trigger.saved: Double Tap listens for it right away. You can change it any time in Double Tap settings.
onboarding.done.heading: You're all set
onboarding.done.lead: Nugget keeps indexing in the background. You can start searching and chatting straight away.
onboarding.done.leadNoAi: Nugget keeps indexing in the background. Search works straight away; chat and drafting start once you choose a model.
onboarding.done.searchable: {count, plural, one {# item is} other {# items are}} indexed and searchable.
onboarding.done.pending: You skipped {count, plural, one {one step} other {# steps}}. Go back to:
onboarding.done.ai.local: AI: a model on this device
onboarding.done.again: You can run setup again from the sidebar.

apps.title: Connected AI apps
apps.description: Let apps such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Cursor answer from what Nugget knows, over MCP. Apps connect on this device only, each with its own token and permissions, and every request goes in the audit log.
apps.emptyBody: Connect an app to let it search your sources and knowledge graph, with the access you choose.
apps.help.step1: Choose a name and what the app may read. Sensitive items stay hidden unless you allow them.
apps.help.step2: Nugget creates a token for that app. Copy it, or copy the ready-made setup for your app.
apps.help.step3: Paste it into the app's MCP settings and restart the app. It shows up here as used once it connects.
apps.help.revokeNote: Revoking an app stops its token working immediately.
apps.revokeDialog.title: Revoke {name}?
apps.revokeDialog.description: The app loses access to Nugget straight away. To connect it again later, create a new token.

connectApp.description: Give an AI app on this device read access to Nugget over MCP. You choose what it can see, and you can revoke it at any time.
connectApp.name: App name

connectApp.allToolsHint: Nugget's MCP tools only read; none change your data.
connectApp.sensitiveOn: This app will be able to read items Nugget marked sensitive, such as messages with financial, health or identity details. Many apps send what they read to a cloud AI model. Only allow this for apps you trust with that.
connectApp.sensitiveOff: Off: items Nugget marked sensitive (financial, health, identity details) are never returned to this app.
connectApp.shownOnce: This token is shown only once. Nugget doesn't keep it in readable form, so it can't show it again. If you lose it, revoke this app and connect it again.
connectApp.noSnippets: Point your app's MCP settings at Nugget and use the token above as its bearer token. Run nuggetd mcp --help for the options.
connectApp.notCopied: You haven't copied the token or a setup snippet. Once you close this, the token can't be shown again.

addSource.microsoft.howTo: How to register a Microsoft app
addSource.microsoft.step1: Open the Microsoft Entra admin center (or the Azure portal) and go to App registrations → New registration.
addSource.microsoft.step2: Give it a name. Under Supported account types, choose Accounts in any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts, or this organizational directory only if you'll enter your tenant below.
addSource.microsoft.step3: Under Authentication → Add a platform, choose Mobile and desktop applications and add the custom redirect URIs http://localhost and http://127.0.0.1. No client secret is needed.
addSource.microsoft.step4: Under API permissions → Add a permission → Microsoft Graph → Delegated permissions, add {scope}, offline_access and User.Read. Some organizations need an admin to grant consent.
addSource.microsoft.step5: Copy the Application (client) ID from the app's Overview page into the field below. For a single-tenant app, also copy the Directory (tenant) ID into Tenant.
addSource.microsoft.oneApp: One app registration can serve Outlook mail, calendar and OneDrive: add Mail.Read, Calendars.Read and Files.Read to it.
addSource.microsoft.privacy: Nugget signs in through your browser and a redirect to this device only. Tokens are kept in your OS keychain and Nugget talks to Microsoft directly.
addSource.microsoft.clientIdHint: From your app registration's Overview page.
addSource.microsoft.clientIdMissing: Paste the Application (client) ID of your app registration.
addSource.microsoft.tenantHint: Leave empty for work, school and personal accounts (common). Or enter organizations, consumers, your tenant ID or a domain like contoso.onmicrosoft.com.
addSource.microsoft.tenantInvalid: Enter common, organizations, consumers, a tenant ID or a domain.
addSource.microsoft.accountHint: Email address to pre-select on Microsoft's sign-in page.
addSource.microsoft.foldersHint: Comma separated: inbox, sentitems, archive… or folder IDs. Empty means Inbox and Sent Items.
addSource.microsoft.foldersInvalid: Use folder names like inbox or archive, or folder IDs.
addSource.microsoft.includeHint: Paths from the top of your OneDrive, comma or newline separated, e.g. /Documents/Work. Empty means the whole drive.
addSource.microsoft.pathInvalid: Use folder paths like /Documents/Work, without . or .. parts.
addSource.microsoft.secretHint: Only for apps registered with the Web platform; desktop apps don't need one. Stored in your OS keychain.

addSource.slack.howTo: How to get a Slack user token
addSource.slack.step1: Open your Slack apps page and choose Create New App → From scratch in your workspace.
addSource.slack.step2: Under OAuth & Permissions → User Token Scopes, add channels:history, channels:read, groups:history, groups:read, im:history, im:read, mpim:history, mpim:read and users:read.
addSource.slack.step3: Choose Install to Workspace (an admin may need to approve it), then copy the User OAuth Token. It starts with xoxp-.
addSource.slack.botToken: That's a bot token. Paste the User OAuth Token, which starts with xoxp-.
addSource.slack.conversationsHint: Channel names or IDs, comma separated, e.g. #general, C0123456789. Empty means your DMs and the channels you're in.
addSource.slack.nothing: Choose direct messages, channels, or list some conversations.
addSource.notion.howTo: How to create a Notion integration
addSource.notion.step1: Open your Notion integrations page and create a New integration of type Internal for your workspace.
addSource.notion.step2: Under Capabilities, Read content is all Nugget needs. Copy the Internal Integration Secret.
addSource.notion.step3: Share pages with it: on each page or database to include, open ••• → Connections and add your integration. Pages inside them are included too.
addSource.notion.databasesHint: Index databases shared with the integration, and their rows.
addSource.github.howTo: How to create a GitHub token
addSource.github.tokenStep1: Open your GitHub token settings and choose Generate new token (fine-grained).
addSource.github.tokenStep2: Choose the repositories to include. Under Repository permissions, set Issues, Pull requests and Discussions to Read-only (Metadata is read-only automatically).
addSource.github.tokenStep3: A classic token works too: give it the repo and read:discussion scopes.
addSource.github.appStep1: Open GitHub's developer settings and create a New OAuth App. Any homepage and callback URL will do; Nugget doesn't use them.
addSource.github.appStep2: Tick Enable Device Flow, register the app and copy its Client ID. No client secret is needed.
addSource.github.appStep3: When you connect, Nugget shows a code. Enter it on GitHub's page and approve read access (repo, read:discussion).
addSource.github.clientIdHint: From your GitHub OAuth App, with the device flow enabled.
addSource.github.reposHint: owner/name, comma separated. Empty means every issue, pull request and discussion you take part in.
addSource.github.reposInvalid: Write repositories as owner/name, e.g. octocat/hello-world.
addSource.github.allActivityHint: Not only the items that involve you.
addSource.linear.howTo: How to create a Linear API key
addSource.linear.tokenStep1: In Linear, open Settings → Security & access and create a personal API key. Read access is enough.
addSource.linear.tokenStep2: Copy the key. It starts with lin_api_.
addSource.linear.appStep1: In Linear, open Settings → API → OAuth applications and create an application.
addSource.linear.appStep3: Copy its Client ID. Nugget asks only for read access and signs in with PKCE, so no client secret is needed.
addSource.linear.teamsHint: Team keys, comma separated, e.g. ENG. Empty means every team.
addSource.linear.teamsInvalid: Team keys are letters and digits, like ENG.
